chosen.premise: Nidoqueen’s back spines never secrete poison while young are nestled between them.
chosen.hook: Nidoqueen’s poisonous defense has one very specific safety switch.
chosen.visualIdea: Show glowing spines changing from toxic purple to safe blue as young appear between them.
chosen.note: An unusually specific biological safety rule, directly stated in the Shield Pokédex entry. The young nestled among the spines create a strong visual reveal.

candidates.premise: When excited, Nidoqueen’s stiff needle-like scales bristle outward instead of remaining flat.
candidates.hook: Excite Nidoqueen, and her armor suddenly points straight at you.
candidates.visualIdea: Start with smooth scales, then snap each needle outward as Nidoqueen’s excitement meter rises.
candidates.note: A clear, animation-friendly transformation directly supported by two entries. It is compelling, but less unexpected than the offspring-specific poison safeguard.

candidates.premise: Nidoqueen uses her rugged body to seal the entrance of her nest against predators.
candidates.hook: Nidoqueen doesn’t just guard the nest—she becomes its door.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Nidoqueen backing into a burrow until her armored body completely blocks the entrance.
candidates.note: The nest-sealing behavior is distinctive and well supported, but “becomes its door” and “completely blocks” are slightly dramatized beyond the wording of the entries.

candidates.premise: Nidoqueen’s protective scales grow in cycles rather than staying permanently unchanged.
candidates.hook: Nidoqueen’s armor doesn’t just grow—it grows in cycles.
candidates.visualIdea: Use a time-lapse armor graphic showing successive rings of scales growing over Nidoqueen’s body.
candidates.note: The cyclic growth detail is directly supported and concrete, though the research gives no timing or mechanism, limiting the visual and explanatory payoff.

candidates.premise: Despite her powerful tackles, Nidoqueen is officially described as better at defense than offense.
candidates.hook: Nidoqueen can send foes flying—and she’s still better at defense.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen between a foe launched by a tackle and Nidoqueen shielding children from incoming attacks.
candidates.note: The offense-versus-defense contradiction is clearly backed by the entries, but the general defensive-warrior framing could fit several armored Pokémon.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required. The episode should center on the offspring-specific safety switch, ideally clarifying that the Pokédex says the spines do not secrete poison while young are present.
